text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Brentford and Nottingham Forest.
Brentford are going through a tough run in the Premier League and have lost seven of their last eight games, including all of their previous five.
As a result, the Bees have slipped from ninth in the table to 16th and are just three points above the relegation zone.

Thomas Frank would have been hoping that the FA Cup third round would have served as a way to turn their form around, but they drew with Wolves before losing 3-2 in extra-time in the replay to extend their dismal run.
However, they have been boosted by the return of striker Ivan Toney, who is back after serving an eight-month ban for breaking betting rules.

There have been plenty of rumours linking the forward with a move away from the club, with many teams in the Premier League interested in his services, but all the focus today will be around his return to action.
Forest have pulled away from the relegation zone by four points after winning back-to-back games in the Premier League.

Fans of the Tricky Trees weren't happy when popular manager Steve Cooper was sacked after their loss to Tottenham, with the club triumphing just once in their last 13 matches under his leadership, but new boss Nuno Espirito Santo has had a positive impact.
Forest were unfortunate to lose 3-2 to Bournemouth in his first fixture in charge before successive victories over Newcastle United and Manchester United.
They were also in FA Cup action in midweek after coming from two goals down to secure a replay against League One Blackpool.
The Tricky Trees were in control after goals from Andrew Omobamidele and Danilo put them ahead, only for Albie Morgan and Kyle Joseph to equal the score for the Tangerines.
However, Forest were too strong for their opponents in extra time, with Chris Wood scoring the winner to send them into a tie against Bristol City in the next round.
Brentford make three changes to the side that lost to Wolves in the FA Cup in midweek.
As expected, Toney starts up front and captains the side after serving an eight-month ban for a breach of betting rules.
As a result, Dasilva moves onto the bench.
Flekken returns in goal, and Pinnock starts at centre-back, with Strakosha and Ajer missing out.
New signing Reguilon, who joined on loan from Tottenham, is among the substitutes.
Bryan Mbeumo, Kevin Schade and Christian Norgaard are out through injury, with Yoane Wissa, Saman Ghoddos and Frank Onyeka on international duty.
Forest make two alterations to the side that beat Blackpool in the FA Cup.
Turner has started the last five matches in the Premier League and comes in for Vlachodimos.
There is also a switch at right-back, with Montiel replacing Williams.
The Tricky Trees have lots of absentees in the squad, with Divock Origi, Felipe, Anthony Elanga and Morgan Gibbs-White all out through injury.
Ola Aina, Ibrahim Sangare, Serge Aurier, Willy Boly, Moussa Niakhate and Cheikhou Kouyate are all missing after being called up to the African Cup of Nations.
Brentford are unbeaten in their last five league meetings with Forest (winning two and drawing three) since a 1-0 home loss in January 2020 in the Championship.
Both teams are on the pitch and are ready to get started.
Forest get this Premier League clash under way.
Yates with the first kick.
Toney makes his return to Brentford's side following his ban from last season.
He’s scored in all three of his league games against Forest, while he’s also scored in each of his last three Premier League games at the Gtech Community Stadium.
Despite scoring 20 top-flight goals last season, it will be interesting to see how he does without Mbeumo, Wissa and Schade, who all played alongside him in the attack in the previous term.
GOALLLL! DANILO SCORES! 1-0 FOREST! What a start for the Tricky Trees! Brentford have had most of the possession, but it has been in their own half.
Janelt's sliced clearance on the edge of the box is headed away by Mee, with the centre-back playing it straight to Danilo.
The Brazilian then takes a touch off his thigh before volleying the ball beyond Flekken.
Forest have won their last two Premier League games, last winning three in a row in the division in May 1999.
Away from home, the Tricky Trees could win successive top-flight outings for the first time since April 1995 under Frank Clark (run of four).
Brentford look to respond quickly with a throw-in on the right.
Forest clear the danger before Janelt thumps an effort well off target.
Yates comes forward with possession down the right of Brentford's half and is not put under any pressure.
He then goes for goal with an effort from range, but he drags his effort well wide of the bottom-left corner.
Forest have gained confidence from their early goal and are playing the ball around with pace inside Brentford's half.
Tavares is getting forward at every opportunity but is being forced back.
Damsgaard does well to win a throw-in on the right and takes it quickly, playing it into the path of Janelt.
He rolls it across to Mee outside the box, but his ambitious low drive from range is blocked.
The Bees are already rushing their chances.
BLOCK! Forest have all the momentum at the moment.
Wood does well to retain possession on the left side of the box and waits for support before playing it back to Yates on the edge.
His low strike is deflected into the path of Hudson-Odoi, who has his shot from close range blocked.
He appeals for handball but nothing is given.
Forest have a corner on the right, with four of their players huddling in the middle to discuss tactics.
The cross reaches the head of Yates, but his flick towards the back of the box comes to nothing.
Nobody was there to get on the end of it.
Brentford have now gone 10 successive Premier League matches without a clean sheet, since a 2-0 win at Chelsea in October last year.
They have only had two shots and must improve if they want to avoid six successive losses.
Mangala is the first player to go into the book after dragging back Damsgaard on the edge of the box.
Toney is over the free-kick.

GOALLLL! TONEY SCORES ON HIS RETURN! 1-1! It really couldn’t be anyone but Toney to score for the Bees! He has a free-kick just outside the box on the right and goes low with his effort, curling the ball into the bottom-right corner.
There was a large space left by the Forest wall and he makes the most of it!
Tavares is over a free-kick just inside the Brentford half, with Forest loading the box.
However, he puts too much height and weight on it, allowing Flekken to catch it with ease.
Toney has only had 11 touches but has scored.
He has had an interesting battle with Murillo, who has dealt with his height and physicality well so far.
Brentford are full of confidence.
Janelt shows some quick feet to beat a defender down the left before winning a corner.
The Bees take it short and work it out to Damsgaard, who drills a cross into the gloves of Turner.
He came off his line well to claim it.
Jensen goes short with a throw-in before getting it back from Damsgaard.
He takes a touch of his feet before curling an inswinging cross towards Maupay on the left, with his header at the near post deflecting out for a corner.
Toney knocks a header into the path of Maupay, who races into the box to try and get a shot away.
However, Murillo matches the run of the striker and uses his strength to push him off the ball.
Mee strolls out of the defence and plays a pass into the path of Maupay, with Omobamidele getting across him to slide it out for a corner.
Summer signing Omobamidele scored on his Forest debut in the FA Cup during the week and is trying to prove himself in the competitive squad.
BAR! Brentford go close to taking the lead.
Jensen's inswinging cross is knocked across the box by Toney.
Yates can't clear it away under pressure, and Lewis-Potter thumps an effort from close range that comes off the underside of the bar before getting cleared away.
The referee checks his watch to make sure that the ball didn't go over the line.
Forest's only shot on target was their goal inside three minutes.
Elanga has been a big miss for the Tricky Trees, who are struggling to create opportunities to score since conceding.
He has four goals and six assists this campaign.
Jensen's long throw-in from the right is headed away by Tavares before it could reach anyone inside the box.
CHANCE! Hudson-Odoi bursts down the left and plays the ball into the path of Mangala, who bursts towards the byline.
He cuts it back to Dominguez, but the midfielder takes a heavy touch, allowing Flekken to claim it.
Tavares surges forward from his left-back position and arrives just outside the Brentford box.
He has options around him but goes for goal from a distance.
His shot moves in the air, but it goes straight at Flekken, who claims it on the second attempt.
Dominguez has possession on the right and he looks to put a cross into the box before sliding a pass into the path of Montiel.
The right-back then blasts a cross into the box that is punched away by Flekken.
The game has been paused after Dominguez and Maupay clash heads.
The medical teams are on the pitch to assess the players.
Dominguez and Maupay are both back on their feet after their heads collided in Brentford's half.
The referee gets the match back under way with Forest in possession.
Damsgaard makes the most of a loose ball on the halfway line and drives forward with the ball before rolling it down the left to Toney.
The crowd call for him to shoot at a near-impossible angle, but he goes for a cross.
However, it is poor, with the ball going straight out for a goal-kick.
Dominguez has a free-kick on the right, but his cross is poor and Toney heads it away.
There will be four minutes of additional time.
Yates is feeling the effects of an early challenge from Mee and hobbles around the pitch before going down.
The medical team are on the pitch to treat the captain.
Yates is back on his feet and seems to be walking freely after finding it difficult a few moments ago.
He is waiting to be allowed back on the pitch.
CHANCE! Toney gets on the end of a quick throw-in and pokes a pass through to Damsgaard on the byline.
He then plays a cutback towards Maupay, but he cannot get a strong contact on his effort and Turner claims.
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-1 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Toney scored on his return to Premier League action to cancel Danilo's opener and send Brentford and Forest into the break with the score 1-1.
The Bees have lost their last five in the top flight and went behind early on when Danilo thumped a volley from outside the box beyond Flekken inside three minutes.
Yates dragged a shot from range well wide of the bottom-left corner, and Hudson-Odoi had an effort from close range blocked before Toney scored.
He curled a free-kick around the wall and into the bottom-right corner, with his last goal also coming through a free-kick against the Tricky Trees.
Brentford were the better side from that point but couldn't make their dominance count.
Lewis-Potter went the closet, thumping the bar with a strike from inside the box.
Forest were the better side in the opening exchanges and gained confidence from Danilo's early opener, but Toney's equaliser forced them to defend for the rest of the half.
They have only created an xG (expected goals) of 0.23 from their six shots and are clearly missing Gibbs-White and Elanga, who are usually mainstays in their attack.
As for Brentford, the introduction of Toney has given them something to aim for up front, with the striker doing well to hold the ball up as well as move into the channels.
Janet has been their busiest player, with the midfielder having 50 touches and 45 passes.
Brentford get the ball rolling again.
No changes were made at the break.
Brentford win an early free-kick on the left in a crossing position.
Jensen's right-footed ball into the box looks for Mee, but Forest do well to clear it away.
Since their return to the Premier League last season, Forest have conceded 29 goals in 12 away league games against London sides, an average of 2.4 per game.
They lost 5-0 against Fulham on their last visit to the capital.
They have only conceded one goal, but they are allowing Brentford to regain the momentum after the half-time break.
The Tricky Trees keep clearing the ball forward at every opportunity and are not showing much composure in possession.
Danilo goes into the book after a late tackle on Collins.
The referee allowed the game to continue before going back to book the Brazilian when the ball went off the pitch.
Damsgaard looks to unleash a quick attack down the right with a ball towards the touchline.
Roerslev rushes forward to try and get on the end of it, but Omobamidele gets across to shield it off the pitch.
CHANCE! Brentford almost turn the score around.
Toney has the ball on the right and he flashes an inviting cross into the box.
Lewis-Potter darts into the box to get on the end of it, but his poked effort goes straight at Turner.
Montiel is the third Forest player to be shown a yellow card after delaying the restart.
WIDE! What an opportunity for Forest.
Danilo has a cross on the left blocked by Roerslev before sliding a low pass into the path of Mangala.
He gets a shot away at a tight angle but flicks it wide.
Roerslev bursts down the right after getting on the end of a pass from Toney and plays a cross into Maupay, who commits two defenders before letting it go through to Lewis-Potter.
However, he rushes his attempt and scuffs the shot well wide.
GOALLL! MEE SCORES! 2-1 BRENTFORD! The Bees come from behind to take the lead.
Jensen's inswinging corner from the right is met by Mee, who rushes towards the near post and powers a header into the top-left corner.
That's a superb cross from Jensen.
He knows where Mee is going to run and finds the centre-back perfectly.
Mee wants it more than Murillo and gets ahead of the defender to score with his head.
Brentford are in the lead, but Frank will know the job is far from done after previous results this campaign.
The Bees have dropped more points from winning positions than any other side in the Premier League this season (20).
They’re also one of six teams yet to win when conceding first.
Nuno has seen enough and has decided to make his first change.
Yates rushes off the pitch and is replaced by Williams, who will take a more advanced position than usual.
Forest need to improve the quality of their play.
Tavares has space and time to deliver a cross into the box from the left, but he cannot get it past Janelt on the edge.
Wood, who hasn't had a shot, must be getting frustrated with the lack of service.
GOAALLLL! WOOD SCORES! 2-2! What a response from Forest.
Danilo battles well to retain the ball outside the box before rolling a pass into Hudson-Odoi.
He shifts possession onto his right foot and curls a cross into Wood, who gets into the middle and heads his downward effort into the bottom-right corner.
What a cross from Hudson-Odoi.
His delivery has both pace and accuracy, allowing Wood to simply redirect the ball past Flekken.
Toney goes into the book for a foul on Mangala in the air.

GOALLLL! MAUPAY SCORES! 3-2 BRENTFORD! The Bees take the lead for a second time! Toney switches the ball over to Roerslev on the right, who takes his time before curling a cross towards Maupay just inside the box.
He twists past a defender to make space before blasting his effort into the bottom-right corner.
There is a VAR check for handball against the striker, but the goal stands.
Roerslev doesn't rush his cross.
He asses his options in the middle before floating a cross over to Maupay.
The Frenchman thinks quickly to get past his marker before finishing emphatically.
Maupay has scored in three consecutive games across all competitions for the first time since December 2021 for Brighton.
It's the first time he's scored in three successive appearances for Brentford since April 2019.
Williams' outswinging corner is headed away by Mee.
The ball goes back out to the Wales international on the right, but his second cross is knocked behind.
Brentford make their first two changes.
Damsgaard has been energetic in the midfield and is given a rest.
Baptiste is on in his place.
Brentford are on their way to their first win in six Premier League outings.
Frank wants to protect their lead, so is making a defensive change.
Reguilon is on for his debut and replaces striker Maupay.
Forest switch the play over to the right with Williams waiting, who drops it back to Montiel.
The Argentina international looks for Wood in the middle, but his cross is poor and Flekken claims it on the ground.
Forest move the ball around quickly on the edge of Brentford's box before Wood's low effort is blocked by Mee.
Dominguez and Danilo rush towards the ball in front of the goal but give away a free-kick.
CLOSE! Dominguez fires a pass down the left side of the box to Wood, who uses his strength to protect the ball from a defender before flicking it inside to Mangala.
He gets a shot away but blasts his effort wide of the left post.
Brentford are sitting in a low block and are making it difficult for Forest.
Hudson-Odoi tries to unlock the defence with some quick feet down the left but is forced to go back before recycling possession.
Baptiste has the ball on the right and he rolls it back to Toney, who lofts a high cross towards the back of the box.
Reguilon is there, but he fails to connect with a volley at the far post.
The Bees retain the possession, with Jensen curling a shot from range straight at Turner.
Forest make their third change.
Montiel is on a yellow card and is coming off for Aguilera.
Roerslev is receiving medical treatment after Tavares accidentally staps on his hand.
The Brentford man looks to be in some serious pain.
Brentford make two late substitutions.
Lewis-Potter will be disappointed that he failed to score from one of his three shots.
He is replaced by Dasilva.
Roerslev cannot continue after picking up an injury a couple of minutes ago and is coming off for Ajer, who is tasked with helping the Bees defend their lead.
There will be 10 minutes of additional time.
Janelt battles to win possession in Forest's half before surging towards the byline.
He protects the ball from Williams and then plays it back to Mee.
Toney does brilliantly to control a throw-in before flicking a pass through to Dasilva.
He beats a defender down the left on his way to the byline before losing possession to Murillo.
Jensen has a deep free-kick in Forest's half, with Brentford deciding to load the box.
He plays a quick pass down the left to Dasilva, who blasts a low cross straight at Danilo and wins a corner.
Jensen has been a threat with his throw-ins and corners but is now on his way off.
Yarmoliuk is given the final few minutes to impress.
Forest have possession in Brentford's half, but the chance is gone when Murillo pulls the ball off the pitch in the final few seconds.
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 3-2 NOTTINGHAM FOREST
Toney marked his return to the Premier League with a goal as Brentford came from behind to beat Forest 3-2.
Danilo opened the scoring with a volley from outside the box inside three minutes, with the Tricky Trees having the best of the early chances.
However, Toney announced his return to football after an eight-month absence with an impressive free-kick, curling his low shot from the edge into the bottom-right corner.
Lewis-Potter then thumped the bar with a strike from close range before an entertaining second half.
Mee powered in Jensen’s corner with his head to give the Bees the lead, with Forest responding soon after.
Hudson-Odoi’s inswinging cross from the right found Wood, who planted his downward header beyond Flekken.
Mangala then went close before Brentford struck the winner.
Roerslev's cross from the right found Maupay, who twisted past his marker on the edge of the box before rocketing his effort into the bottom-right corner.
The Bees' first win in six league outings puts them six points ahead of the relegation zone.
They go to Tottenham in the top flight for their next match.
As for Forest, they travel to Bristol City in the FA Cup.
That's all, goodbye.
